target.title: perf(azure): accelerate snapshot lifecycle
target.body:
## Why

Azure Windows snapshot forks remove machine bootstrap from the critical path, but the remaining Azure resource lifecycle still dominates short desktop-test runs. Snapshot and restored-disk storage also need an explicit performance choice instead of inheriting Azure defaults that may optimize for cost rather than fork latency.

This PR keeps Crabbox's existing defaults unchanged while adding an opt-in low-latency path and shortening the independent Azure create/delete work around each snapshot-backed lease.

## What Changed

- Add `azure.snapshotSKU` / `--azure-snapshot-sku` for checkpoint storage and `azure.osDiskSKU` / `--azure-os-disk-sku` for restored managed disks.
- Validate snapshot SKUs against Azure's supported snapshot values and restored-disk SKUs against the Azure SDK's managed-disk values.
- Create snapshot-fork networking and the restored OS disk concurrently, canceling sibling work on failure and preserving all errors.
- Set VM attachment delete options so snapshot-fork NICs and OS disks are owned by the VM lifecycle.
- Request force deletion for the VM, delete its remaining NIC, public IP, and OS disk concurrently, and verify the VM, NIC, public IP, OS disk, and snapshot-quarantine NSG are absent before reporting success.
- Document the opt-in `Premium_LRS` checkpoint and restored-disk configuration.

## Verification

Current landing candidate: `c2e096420c0dd33fd56882340c390f36e45233a4`, restacked onto landed Azure Windows snapshot support `db25e4a62cf4613161f67ff8284e3bb196ce6a19`.

- `go test -race ./internal/cli ./internal/providers/azure`
- `go vet ./...`
- focused SKU, concurrent prerequisite, CLI flag, and provider rewrite coverage
- whole-branch autoreview clean at 0.82 confidence
- exact-head CI: Go, Apple VZ, Worker, Scripts, Docs, and Release Check green

## Live Azure Proof

Exact-head proof on `c2e096420c0dd33fd56882340c390f36e45233a4`:

- Acquired source lease `cbx_b8a811058d64` as an on-demand `Standard_D4s_v4` Azure Windows desktop; stable SSH and loopback VNC were ready in 6m9.866s.
- Created checkpoint `chk_31d2553cb4aa7ddb` in 135.01s. Azure reported the snapshot as `Premium_LRS`/Succeeded, and the source returned to ready after its bounded deallocate/snapshot/restart cycle.
- Forked lease `cbx_e10cbd07343c` while omitting `--desktop`; it inherited desktop capability and reached ready in 168.73s with a `Premium_LRS` restored OS disk.
- During concurrent prerequisite creation, the restored disk was already `Premium_LRS`/Succeeded while the NIC remained attached to the lease-scoped priority-100 deny-all NSG and public SSH was blocked. After rehydration, the temporary NSG was gone and the NIC used the shared SSH allowlist.
- Authenticated `crabbox screenshot` over the SSH-forwarded loopback VNC endpoint produced a clean Windows desktop locally; public TCP 5900 remained blocked and the image was not uploaded.
- Deleted the fork in 30.30s. The command verified deletion before success, and Azure immediately reported zero resources with the fork lease tag. Deleted the source and checkpoint; final Crabbox inventory, canary-tagged Azure resources, and snapshot inventory were all empty.

## Stack

1. [https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/pull/698](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/pull/698) Azure Windows snapshot forks (landed)
2. [https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/pull/731](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/pull/731) Azure snapshot lifecycle performance (this PR)
